entries.test: Public evaluations of Grok 3's general capabilities and comparisons with contemporary leading models would test the stated capability claims.
entries.note: “It wasn’t” most directly rejects the immediately preceding AGI prediction; explicitly rejecting both claims expands that commitment.
“Looked like” expresses an evaluative impression, which the proposition turns into an unqualified claim of copying. Benchmark results and compute usage are separately checkable components.
He reports what he personally noticed, not the absence of all originality. Public evidence cannot establish his private perception.
Marcus adopts the tentative conclusion while attributing its supporting data to an OpenAI employee.

entries.test: The launch recording and accompanying benchmark disclosures would establish whether full o3 was compared and how many benchmarks were reported.
entries.note: The proposition appropriately omits his speculative explanation about access.
The competitive reassurance is clear in context, but no shared threshold defines a threat major enough to invalidate it.
Neither “game changer” nor “major leap” supplies a shared criterion for the magnitude or type of improvement.

entries.test: Reproducible public tests showing Grok 3 generating fabricated factual assertions would establish that hallucinations persist.
entries.note: “Magically” is rhetorical emphasis on an otherwise factual claim.

entries.test: Public comparisons over time of rival models' capabilities, prices, and availability would show whether competitors were closing OpenAI's competitive advantage.
entries.note: In context, the moat refers to OpenAI's competitive advantage as rival models become comparable.

entries.test: Public model pricing histories and providers' explanations of competitive price cuts would show whether price competition continued as OpenAI's advantage narrowed.
entries.note: This is an undated firm forecast with a causal explanation, rather than an explicit if-then condition.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures for competing AI businesses and Nvidia would show whether profits remained elusive across the former while Nvidia remained profitable.
entries.note: “Out of reach” is stronger than “elusive,” and “every AI company” broadens the contextual scope. The source does not explicitly make continuing price wars an antecedent.

entries.test: Public training disclosures and broad capability evaluations of systems available by publication would establish whether pure pretraining scaling had produced general human-level intelligence.
entries.note: This concerns achievement by publication, not whether pretraining scaling could ever produce AGI.

entries.test: Public evaluations comparing Grok 3 with o3 and testing broad general capabilities would establish its competitiveness, AGI limitations, and relative performance.
entries.note: The clause explicitly summarizes Karpathy's conclusions. Marcus signals agreement, but “in many ways similar” does not unambiguously adopt every component as his own.
